title: Also At vs Hdfc Bank Limited on 10 April, 2023
full_text: Also At vs Hdfc Bank Limited on 10 April, 2023 DLND010022162016 IN THE COURT OF ADDITIONAL DISTRICT JUDGE- 01, NEW DELHI DISTRICT, PATIALA HOUSE COURTS, NEW DELHI Presided over by :- MS. VIJETA SINGH RAWAT (DHJS) Arbitration No. 13242/16 H M Informatics Private Limited Through Its Director Sh. Manoj Kaul, Office at : E-3/12, GRD Floor, Bank Side Corner, Malviya Nagar, New Delhi - 110017 Also At : H M Informatics Private Limited Through its Director Manoj Kaul Office at : Shop no. 4, IN 265, Ground floor, Hakikat Nagar, Kingsway Camp, Delhi - 110009 ......... Petitioner Versus HDFC Bank Limited Ansal Classique Tower, 9th floor, J block, Community Centre, Rajouri Garden, New Delhi - 110027 Arbitration No. 13242/16 H M Informatics Pvt. Ltd. vs. HDFC Bank Ltd.. Page no. 1 of 14 Also at : HDFC Bank Ltd Having branch office at : G-4, Ground Floor, Suryakiran building 19 K.G. Marg, New Delhi ........ Respondent Petition presented On : 02.04.2016 Arguments Concluded On : 20.02.2023 Judgment Pronounced On : 10.04.2023 JUDGMENT 1. By way of this judgment, the Court proposes to decide petition u/s 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 (hereinafter referred to as the " Arbitration Act ") whereby the petitioner has challenged award dated 29.11.2014 (hereinafter referred to as the "Impugned Award"), passed by Ld. Sole Arbitrator Justice (Retd.) Rajesh Rai in Arbitration Case no. HDFC/ARB (SECURED/1460), initiated pursuant to a reference made by the respondent against the petitioner. 2. Shorn of unnecessary details facts of the case, as expounded from a perusal of the pleadings and case record are as under:- a) Pursuant to several rounds of discussion that ensued between the petitioner and the respondent, a car loan agreement bearing no. 23901321 dated 18.03.2013 (hereinafter referred to as the "Loan Agreement") for a sum of Rs.6,16,000/- (Rupees Six Lakhs Sixteen Thousand only) was entered between the petitioner and the respondent. Pertinently, as per the Loan Agreement, the respondent sanctioned and disbursed the said Arbitration No. 13242/16 H M Informatics Pvt. Ltd. vs. HDFC Bank Ltd.. Page no. 2 of 14 amount to enable the petitioner to purchase SKODA RAPID 1.6 MPI ELEGANCE bearing registration no. DL11CA0769, Engine no. CLS082970 and chassis no. TMBBDKNA6BG010259. Notably, as per the Loan Agreement, the sanctioned amount was agreed to be paid by the petitioner to the respondent as per Clause 2, thereof. At the same time, in terms of the provisions under Clauses 1.22 and 5 of the Loan Agreement, the petitioner had hypothecated the aforesaid vehicle with the respondent. It is the case of the respondent that after availing the loan facility, the petitioner failed to adhere with the financial discipline and committed willful default in the loan account. Consequent whereupon, the respondent invoked the Arbitration clause as contained under the Loan Agreement, which culminated into the passing of the impugned award. b) Relevantly, the petitioner while approaching this Court by means of the present petition has primarily harped upon its unawareness of the initiation of the aforesaid arbitration proceedings and the passing of the impugned award. In fact, in order to buttress its arguments, the petitioner has sought to take a refuge to another arbitration proceedings initiated at the behest of the respondent in relation to another loan agreement for a sum of Rs.7,39,500/- (Rupees Seven Lakhs Thirty Nine Thousand and Five Hundred only), for the petitioner's purchase of SKODA RAPID 1.6 MPI ELEGANCE MT bearing registration no. DL8CZ0427. Pertinently, as per the petitioner the respondent had initiated proceedings in terms of Section 9 of the Arbitration Act bearing Arbitration petition no. 61/14 before the Ld. Additional District Judge, Tis Hazari Courts in relation to the said loan facility. The petitioner has further contended that in the instant Arbitration No. 13242/16 H M Informatics Pvt. Ltd. vs. HDFC Bank Ltd.. Page no. 3 of 14 proceedings the Court vide its ex-parte order dated 22.08.2014, inter-alia, appointed the Authorized Representative of the respondent as a receiver to take into custody, the vehicle bearing registration no. DL8CZ0427. It is further a case of the petitioner that subsequent to the passing of the said order, the arbitration proceedings commenced between the petitioner and the respondent. Consequently, during the course of proceedings held on 27.09.2014 in Arbitration petition no. 61/14, the respondent had inter alia undertaken not to dispose of the said vehicle till the culmination of the said arbitration proceedings. c) The petitioner in its instant petition has further averred that it joined the aforesaid arbitration proceedings. However, despite the respondent as well as the Ld. Sole Arbitrator being aware of the pendency of another arbitration proceedings, from which the instant petition has emanated, failed to inform the petitioner regarding the same. Needless to mention, the petitioner has also averred regarding non-compliance of aforementioned order dated 27.09.2014 by the respondent and a contempt proceedings initiated at the behest of the petitioner in relation thereto, which are not germane to the determination of the present proceedings. d) Appositely, it is the petitioner's further case that its awareness of the passing of the impugned award arose only when the petitioner received a notice in arbitration proceedings no. 240/2015 from the Court of Ms. Vineeta Goyal, Ld. ADJ, PHC, NDD, filed by the respondent u/s 9 of the Arbitration Act seeking appointment of a Court receiver to take possession of vehicle bearing registration no. DL11CA0769. Notably, the said petition was dismissed by the Ld. ADJ vide order dated 08.02.2016 inter- Arbitration No. 13242/16 H M Informatics Pvt. Ltd. vs. HDFC Bank Ltd.. Page no. 4 of 14 alia, under the observation that the impugned award can straightway be executed in accordance with Section 36 of the Arbitration Act. 3. Consequent thereupon, and in light of the aforesaid facts and circumstances, the petitioner has approached this Court by means of present petition challenging the impugned award under the following grounds:- i) That the impugned order is non-est in the eyes of law as no service was made upon the petitioner and the arbitrator proceeded ex-parte against the petitioner without firstly, satisfying that there was no proof of service upon the petitioner. ii) The arbitrator has accepted the documents of the respondent as sacrosanct without directing the respondent to establish the case on merits. iii) That the arbitration proceedings were conducted in a fraudulent and suspicious manner without affording the petitioner an opportunity of presenting his case. Further, the petitioner never received any notice from the arbitrator and no proof of service was annexed. iv) That the respondent failed to disclose the total default as per the record of the respondent and a mere statement regarding the petitioner's failure to adhere with the financial discipline was considered by the arbitrator while passing the impugned award. 4. The respondent in its reply to the instant petition has primarily, challenged the invocation of this Court's jurisdiction U/s 34 of the Arbitration Act on the grounds of limitation. At the same time the respondent has outrightly averred that the Arbitration No. 13242/16 H M Informatics Pvt. Ltd. vs. HDFC Bank Ltd.. Page no. 5 of 14 petitioner has deliberately mixed up the facts of two different proceedings, emanating out of two different loan agreements constituting separate and independent transactions. The respondent has further contended that the averment of the petitioner regarding alleged non service of notice of initiation of the instant arbitration proceedings is belied from the records of the arbitration proceedings. Lastly, the respondent has vehemently contended that the petitioner's allegation regarding the arbitrator having reached wrong conclusion basis erroneous appreciation of circumstances/evidence which can not be a subject of scrutiny in instant proceedings which is limited in its scope. 5. Arguments have been heard on behalf of the respective parties and record has been perused. 6. Before proceeding to decide on the rival contentions of the parties, this Court deems it appropriate to remind itself of the scope of powers U/s 34 of the Arbitration Act . It has been very recently held in Delhi Airport Metro Express Pvt. Ltd. Vs. Delhi Metro Rail Corporation Ltd. Civil Appeal no. 5627 of 2021, Arising out of SLP (C) no. 4115 of 2019 decided on 09.09.2021 as under: '...22. A cumulative reading of the UNCITRAL Model Law and Rules, the legislative intent with which the 1996 Act is made, Section 5 and Section 34 of the 1996 Act would make it clear that judicial interference with the arbitral awards is limited to the grounds in Section 34 . While deciding applications filed under Section 34 of the Act, courts are mandated to strictly act in accordance with and within the confines of Section 34 , refraining from appreciation or re-appreciation of matters of fact as well as law. (See: Uttarakhand Purv Sainik Kalyan Arbitration No. 13242/16 H M Informatics Pvt. Ltd. vs. HDFC Bank Ltd.. Page no. 6 of 14 Nigam Limited. v. Northern Coal Field Limited. 1, Bhaven Construction Through Authorised Signatory Premjibhai K. Shah v. Executive Engineer Sardar Sarovar Narmada Nigam Ltd. and Another2 and Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Limited v. Dewan Chand Ram Saran3 ).' 7. It is further pertinent to refer to the decision of Supreme Court in South East Asia Marine Engineering and Constructions Ltd. (SEAMEC Ltd.) Vs. Oil India Ltd , 2021 I AD (S.C.) 192, explicitly enunciated the scope of intervention by Court in proceedings U/s 34 of Arbitration Act . In this regard, the Hon'ble Court held; 12. It is a settled position that a Court can set aside the award only on the grounds as provided in the Arbitration Act as interpreted by the Courts. Recently, this Court in Dyna Technologies Pvt. Ltd. v. Crompton Greaves Ltd. [2019 SCC Online SC 1656] laid down the scope of such interference. This Court observed as follows "26. There is no dispute that Section 34 of the Arbitration Act limits a challenge to an award only on the grounds provided therein or as interpreted by various Courts. We need to be cognizant of the fact that arbitral awards should not be interfered with in a casual and cavalier manner, unless the Court comes to a conclusion that the perversity of the award goes to the root of the matter without there being a possibility of alternative interpretation which may sustain the arbitral award. Section 34 is different in its approach and cannot be equated with a normal appellate jurisdiction. The mandate under Section 34 is to respect the finality of the arbitral award and the party autonomy to get their dispute adjudicated by an alternative forum as provided under the law. If the Courts were to interfere with the arbitral award in the usual course on factual aspects, then the commercial wisdom behind opting for alternate dispute resolution would stand frustrated." (emphasis supplied) 13. It is also settled law that where two views are possible, the Court cannot interfere in the plausible view 1 (2020) 2 SCC 455 2 2021 SCC OnLine SC 8 3 (2012) 5 SCC 306 Arbitration No. 13242/16 H M Informatics Pvt. Ltd. vs. HDFC Bank Ltd.. Page no. 7 of 14 taken by the arbitrator supported by reasoning. This Court in Dyna Technologies (supra) observed as under "27. Moreover, umpteen number of judgments of this Court have categorically held that the Courts should not interfere with an award merely because an alternative view on facts and interpretation of contract exists. The Courts need to be cautious and should defer to the view taken by the Arbitral Tribunal even if the reasoning provided in the award is implied unless such award portrays perversity unpardonable under Section 34 of the Arbitration Act." (emphasis supplied) 8. Reverting to the facts of the present case, the first issue that needs to be decided is whether the present petition u/s 34 of the Arbitration Act has been filed within limitation. Section 34(3) of the Arbitration Act stipulates as under : '...(3) An application for setting aside may not be made after three months have elapsed from the date on which the party making that application had received the arbitral award or, if a request had been made under section 33 , from the date on which that request had been disposed of by the arbitral tribunal: Provided that if the Court is satisfied that the applicant was prevented by sufficient cause from making the application within the said period of three months it may entertain the application within a further period of thirty days, but not thereafter.' 9. In this regard, this court outrightly, observes that the petitioner in its instant petition has averred that it was made aware of the passing of the impugned award only pursuant to the arbitration proceedings bearing no. 240/2015, initiated by the respondent in terms of the provisions u/s 9 of the Arbitration Act before Ms. Vineeta Goyal, Ld. Additional District Judge, Patiala House Court, New Delhi District. In contrast, the respondent despite raising an objection regarding the instant petition being time barred in its reply, failed to demonstrate from any documents or lead any arguments in furtherance of the said Arbitration No. 13242/16 H M Informatics Pvt. Ltd. vs. HDFC Bank Ltd.. Page no. 8 of 14 arguments. Clearly, since the respondent has failed to lead any evidence in support of its contention that the petitioner was timely served with a copy of the impugned award and despite which the petitioner failed to invoke the jurisdiction of this Court, this Court is not inclined to outrightly brush aside the contention of the petitioner regarding it being made aware of the impugned award only during the course of the aforesaid arbitration proceedings bearing no. 240/2015. Accordingly, since the respondent has failed to demonstrate the present petition is time barred, this Court is not in a position to give any conclusion in favour of the respondent and against the petitioner in so far as the issue of limitation is concerned. 10. Secondly, as noted above, the crux and contention of the petitioner's challenge to the impugned award is premised on the alleged ground of non service of notice of initiation of the instant arbitration proceedings upon the petitioner leading to the culmination of ex-parte impugned award. Pertinently in order to determine the said issue, this court vide its order dated 18.08.2022 directed the Ld. Sole Arbitrator Sh. Rajesh Rai, to place on record, original records pertaining to the instant arbitration proceedings. Consequently, upon the said record being filed before this court and upon perusal thereof, this Court observes that the Ld. Sole Arbitrator had issued the following notices to the petitioner regarding the instant arbitration proceedings: a) Notice dated 08.09.2014 issued to the petitioner, the respondent and one Mr. Manoj Kaul R/o Plot no.5/656, Sector 5, Vaishali, Ghaziabad, U.P-201001; Arbitration No. 13242/16 H M Informatics Pvt. Ltd. vs. HDFC Bank Ltd.. Page no. 9 of 14 b) Notice dated 22.09.2014 issued to the petitioner and Mr. Manoj Kaul; c) Notice dated 06.10.2014 issued to the petitioner and Mr. Manoj Kaul; and d) Notice dated 20.10.2014 issued to the petitioner and Mr. Manoj Kaul. 11. Pertinently, from a further perusal of the original Registered AD and tracking receipts of the proof of delivery of the aforesaid notices, as exiting in the arbitral records, it has been noted by this Court that all the aforesaid notices, when issued by the Ld. Sole Arbitrator to the petitioner's address bearing; E-3/12, Grd. Floor, Backside Corner, Malviya Nagar, New Delhi-110017 were returned under the remarks, "Unclaimed". In contrast, the said notices, when issued to the petitioner at its address bearing; Shop No. 4 in 265, Ground Floor, Hakikat Nagar, Kingsway Camp, Delhi-11000 were consistently returned under the remarks, "Delivery Attempted: Insufficient Address". Significantly, this Court has further noted that while the notice dated 08.09.2014, issued to Mr. Manoj Kaul at address bearing; Plot No. 5/656, Sector-5, Vaishali, Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh-201001 was returned under the remarks, "Delivery Attempted: Addressee cannot be located", however, the notice dated 22.09.2014 was duly delivered to the Mr. Manoj Kaul. Further, subsequent notices dated 06.10.2014 and 20.10.2014 were both returned from the said address of Mr. Manoj Kaul under the remarks, "Unclaimed". Needless to mention, perusal of the arbitral records further demonstrate that the said notices were all issued to the addresses of the petitioner and Mr. Manoj Kaul, as specified Arbitration No. 13242/16 H M Informatics Pvt. Ltd. vs. HDFC Bank Ltd.. Page no. 10 of 14 under the Loan Agreement. Further, the said addressees also admittedly correspond with the petitioner's addresses, as specified under the memo of parties to the present petition. 12. In order to further comprehensively deal with the instant point of contention, this Court considers it pertinent to refer Section 27 of the General Clauses Act, 1897, which provides as under; '...27. Meaning of service by post.--Where any Central Act or Regulation made after the commencement of this Act authorizes or requires any document to be served by post, whether the expression "serve" or either of the expressions "give" or "send" or any other expression is used, then, unless a different intention appears, the service shall be deemed to be effected by properly addressing, pre-paying and posting by registered post, a letter containing the document, and, unless the contrary is proved, to have been effected at the time at which the letter would be delivered in the ordinary course of post.' 13. In continuation of the aforesaid, this Court finds its pertinent to refer to the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in K. Bhaskaran v. Sankaran Vaidhyan Balan & Anr. , 1999 VII AD (S.C.) 417, wherein it was, inter alia, held; '...24. No doubt Section 138 of the Act does not require that the notice should be given only by `post'. Nonetheless the principle incorporated in Section 27 (quoted above) can profitably be imported in a case where the sender has despatched the notice by post with the correct address written on it. Then it can be deemed to have been served on the sendee unless he proves that it was not really served and that he was not responsible for such non- service. Any other interpretation can lead to a very tenuous position as the drawer of the cheque who is liable to pay the amount would resort to the strategy of subterfuge by successfully avoiding the notice. 25. Thus, when a notice is returned by the sendee as unclaimed such date would be the commencing date in reckoning the period of 15 days contemplated in clause (c) to the proviso of Section 138 of the Act. Of course Arbitration No. 13242/16 H M Informatics Pvt. Ltd. vs. HDFC Bank Ltd.. Page no. 11 of 14 such reckoning would be without prejudice to the right of the drawer of the cheque to show that he had no knowledge that the notice was brought to his address. In the present case the accused did not even attempt to discharge the burden to rebut the aforesaid presumption." (emphasis supplied)' 14. Similarly, Delhi High Court in Ashwani Kumar Julka (Shri) Vs. Lt. Col . Parthojit Choudhary (Retd.),2006 IX AD (DELHI) 791 while referring to the aforesaid decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, inter alia, observed as under; '...12. At this stage, it would be also of significance to refer to another judgment of the Supreme Court in the case of K. Bhaskaran v. Sankaran Vaidhyan Balan and Anr. . Clauses (b) and (c) of proviso to Section 138 specifically came up for discussion in the said case. Notice sent to the drawer had been returned "unclaimed"- almost similar position as in the instant case. The Court held that when such a notice sent to the addressee at correct address is received back unclaimed, notice can be deemed to have been served on sendee unless he proves that it was never actually served and that he was not responsible for non-service...' 15. Clearly, the principles emanating from the conjoint reading of the aforesaid is that once any notice notice is properly addressed to a party and the same is returned as unclaimed, it may be treated as deemed service under law. Therefore, while applying the said principles to the facts of the present case, it is noted that in the present case, the sole arbitrator had issued several notices, as aforementioned, to the petitioner and Mr. Manoj Kaul at the addresses which were furnished by the said parties under the Loan Agreement. Further, this court has outrightly noted from the records that the said notices were all returned unclaimed from the address bearing; E-3/12, Grd. Floor, Backside Corner, Malviya Nagar, New Delhi-110017 of the petitioner. Therefore, in light of Arbitration No. 13242/16 H M Informatics Pvt. Ltd. vs. HDFC Bank Ltd.. Page no. 12 of 14 the settled principle under law, this Court is left with no option than to conclude that the petitioner was duly served/ deemed served notice of the instant arbitration proceedings. There is no material adduced by the petitioner to show that either it was not available at the addresses or that it was not responsible for non- service. However, despite the same, the petitioner avoided to appear before the arbitrator. Accordingly, the petitioner is precluded from raising any contention regarding non-service of notice of the said proceedings, belatedly before this Court, which contention even stands belied from the documents placed on record. Even otherwise, presuming that the petitioner was unaware of the present arbitration proceedings as vehemently contended before this Court, as noted above, Mr. Manoj Kaul, being one of the Co-borrower under the Loan Agreement, was in due receipt of the notice of the Ld. Sole Arbitrator, dated 22.09.2014 and subsequent notices 06.10.2014 and 20.10.2014, deemed served on Mr. Manoj Kaul. Accordingly, this Court is left with no option than to reject the contention of the petitioner regarding non service of notice of arbitral proceedings on these counts. 16. Lastly, while dealing with the objection of the petitioner regarding the Ld. Sole Arbitrator's non consideration of merits of the case as well as alleged respondent's failure to establish it case on record is concerned, this Court in light of the decisions in Delhi Airport Metro Express pvt. Ltd. (Supra) and South East Asia Marine Engineering and Construction Ltd. (Supra), is not inclined to rule in favour of the petitioner. In this regard, it is noted from the arbitral record that the Ld. Sole Arbitrator has Arbitration No. 13242/16 H M Informatics Pvt. Ltd. vs. HDFC Bank Ltd.. Page no. 13 of 14 reached his conclusions on the basis of documents produced by the respondent, duly proved by its witnesses and unrebutted due to the willful absence of the petitioner. Accordingly, in consonance with the settled principle of law, that the decision of an arbitrator is not subject to interference merely for the reason of a plausible alternative view on fact and interpretation of documents. Accordingly, this argument of the petitioner, too falls short to convince this Court to set aside the impugned award. Needless to reiterate any such interference in arbitral award based on analysis on merits would fall foul of the scope and purview if proceedings under Section 34 of the Arbitration Act. 17. In view of the above discussions, the petition is dismissed. 18. File be consigned to records. Pronounced in open Court (Vijeta Singh Rawat) on 10.04.2023 Additional District Judge-01, New Delhi District, Patiala House Courts, New Delhi Arbitration No. 13242/16 H M Informatics Pvt. Ltd. vs. HDFC Bank Ltd.. Page no. 14 of 14
